title: Spot Phishing and Payment Scams
blurb: Pause, verify, and protect your login and money.
cards: i
Scams create pressure
Unexpected messages may pretend to be a bank, delivery company, employer or friend. Urgency, secrecy, strange links and requests for codes are warning signs.
i
Verify out of band
Do not use the link or phone number in a suspicious message. Open the official app or type a known address yourself, then contact the organization through its published channel.
i
Protect security codes
Never share passwords, PINs or one-time codes with a caller or message sender. A real-looking logo or caller ID can be faked.
d
A message says your account closes in ten minutes
Choose what to do.
Open the official app yourself and check for alerts
You avoid the message link and check through a known channel.
Click its link and enter your password
A suspicious link can lead to a fake sign-in page.
Reply with the one-time code
Codes can let someone access your account.
Pay a fee with gift cards
Gift cards are not a safe way to pay a claimed bank fee.
q
What is the safest way to check a surprising bank message?
Click its link
Use the bank's official app or contact details you already trust
Reply with your PIN
Call the number in the message
Verify separately through a known official channel.
q
A caller asks for the code just sent to your phone. What should you do?
Read it out
Refuse and end the call, then contact the organization independently
Send a screenshot
Give a different code
One-time codes are for you to use; sharing them can let someone access your account.
example: A message warns that a parcel is stuck and asks for a small card payment. Check the delivery company using its official app or website, not the message link.
